A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EFI-PINN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite added material and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Poisson and Black-Scholes simulations and analyses of tumor-growth and scratch-assay data in Sections 4–5 and Appendix A5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Concrete Dropout results and computational timing measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the double-network construction, energy objective, narrow-neck architecture and fiducial inference procedure are retained. Concrete Dropout is an added comparator; the discussion of transfer learning does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: The Poisson variants, Black-Scholes simulations, tumor-growth data and scratch-assay data are retained. The added baseline and timing study use the existing Poisson task. The newly cited treatment-effect application belongs to other work.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds an evaluated Concrete Dropout baseline that learns its dropout rate. All previously evaluated comparators remain; conformal prediction and deep ensembles are discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: New Table A6 introduces a timing comparison using total and per-epoch time, 200,000 epochs for dropout PINN and EFI, 100,000 for B-PINN, and two EFI hyper-network configurations. Existing accuracy-study settings and Appendix A6 hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A5.3 adds a limited computational analysis comparing methods and EFI hyper-networks [16,16,16] and [16,16,4]. Existing noise-level, sample-size, network-size and identifiability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New checklist item 7 explicitly states that experiments use 100 repetitions with randomly chosen seeds. The existing 100-run averages and uncertainty summaries are retained; this adds seed information without establishing increased runs or a new significance test.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Concrete Dropout results: MSE 0.000184, coverage 0.1185 and interval width 0.003706. New Table A6 reports 133 seconds for dropout PINN, 1330 for B-PINN and 391/385 for the two EFI configurations. Matched pre-existing result tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, the fiducial-density derivations and Appendix A4 assumptions and proofs are unchanged. Renaming boundary observations from g to b is a notation edit.

C1.justification: The abstract, headline contributions and conclusion are retained. The introduction adds a comparative claim that EFI's theoretically supported parameter uncertainty, alongside predictive uncertainty, distinguishes it from conformal prediction, deep ensembles and stochastic deep learning.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Concrete Dropout's undercoverage as underestimated uncertainty and discusses EFI's computational cost relative to dropout and HMC. It also elaborates the proposed transfer-learning strategy by suggesting hyper-networks for only the final model layers; the small-model limitation was already acknowledged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 adds a Concrete Dropout code-source link, and Table A6 documents timing, epoch counts and hyper-network sizes. The checklist adds a statement locating source code in supplementary material. Existing detailed hyperparameter tables are preserved; actual external code availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Concrete Dropout, conformal prediction, deep ensembles and EFI treatment-effect inference. A new related-work paragraph expands the comparison between predictive and parameter uncertainty, while retaining the previous research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Related Work heading, a computation-time subsection, keywords, acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. Citation style, author affiliation and boundary notation change, but most prose and the main section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds a comparator row and removes its redundant architecture column; Table A6 is new, and Figure 1 is enlarged and repositioned. Figure 3's right panel is replaced by the existing 18,000-cell panel from Figure A12(e), rather than a newly reported experiment. Other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The learned-dropout comparison and timing study modestly strengthen empirical comparison and computational transparency while preserving the existing method, theory and results. These gains are limited by missing hardware context and unreconciled presentation: Figure 3 reuses an appendix panel while its different-setting explanation remains, and the shortest-interval claim is retained despite Concrete Dropout's narrower intervals.
